query: Which method can be used for oxidation resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Subjecting the equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy to stationary friction processing to induce an ultrafine-grain microstructure will enhance its oxidation resistance by promoting the formation of protective oxide scales.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy with coarse grains (~98 μm) and a BCC/B2 dominant microstructure.
generation.intervention: Stationary friction processing using a WC-cylindrical tool at rotational speeds of 400 rpm or 1800 rpm for 5 minutes.
generation.conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at temperatures of 850 °C (and up to 1050 °C) for 100 hours.
generation.structural_mediator: The reduction in grain size to approximately 1 μm (for 400 rpm) or 0.43 μm (for 1800 rpm), leading to an increased density of grain boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The higher grain boundary density facilitates rapid outward diffusion of Cr, which in turn promotes the formation of a dense, protective Cr2O3 layer followed by an Al-rich oxide formation via inward oxygen diffusion, limiting the formation of nonprotective spinel oxides.
generation.predicted_outcome: The processed samples will exhibit a significant decrease in oxidation kinetics (with reductions up to ~38–48% at higher processing speeds) and lower cumulative mass gains relative to the as‐cast samples. Additionally, a higher activation energy for oxidation is anticipated in the processed samples.
generation.baseline: The as-cast alloy that has a coarse grain structure, leading to a higher oxidation rate, nonprotective oxide formation (e.g., spinels), and lower activation energy for oxidation.
generation.boundary: This hypothesis applies to the specific conditions of the AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy processed via stationary friction processing for 5 minutes at the mentioned rotational speeds and exposed to isothermal oxidation in air at temperatures between 850 and 1050 °C. Outcomes may differ outside these parameters.
generation.uncertainty: While available evidence supports the enhancement of oxidation resistance through grain refinement, the scalability of this approach and the long-term stability of the protective oxide scales under varying operational conditions remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two batches of AlCoCrFeNi alloy samples: one as-cast and another processed by stationary friction processing (using both 400 rpm and 1800 rpm conditions). Subject both batches to isothermal oxidation in air at controlled temperatures (850 °C, 950 °C, and 1050 °C) for 100 hours.
measurements: Mass gain measurements over time to assess oxidation kinetics
Estimation of activation energy for oxidation
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the processed samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in oxidation kinetics (lower mass gain and k_p) and fail to predominantly form protective oxide layers (Cr2O3 and Al-rich oxides) compared to the as-cast samples, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: Paper card. Question: How does an ultrafine-grain microstructure, obtained via stationary friction processing, affect the oxidation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy?. System: Equimolar AlCoCrFeNi high entropy alloy (HEA). Processing: Stationary friction processing (SFP) using a WC-cylindrical tool (12 mm diameter) at rotational speeds of 400 rpm and 1800 rpm for 5 min duration. Test conditions: Isothermal oxidation in laboratory air at 850, 950, and 1050 °C for 100 h. Findings: Grain size refined from 98 μm (as-cast) to 1 μm (SFP_400) and 0.43 μm (SFP_1800).; Phase transformation from BCC/B2 to FCC occurred, with 38% and 55% FCC fraction for SFP_400 and SFP_1800, respectively.; Surface free energy increased by 29.8% for SFP_400 and 35.2% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Oxidation kinetics decelerated by 12–20% for SFP_400 and 38–48% for SFP_1800 compared to as-cast.; Cumulative mass gain at 850 °C after 100 h was 0.33 mg/cm² (as-cast), 0.27 mg/cm² (SFP_400), and 0.17 mg/cm² (SFP_1800).; Parabolic rate constants (k_p) at 1050 °C were 23.2 × 10⁻¹³ g²·cm⁻⁴·s⁻¹ (as-cast), 18.4 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_400), and 8.16 × 10⁻¹³ (SFP_1800).; Processed samples formed predominantly protective
